結婚人數斷崖式下跌：數據揭示的嚴峻現狀

作者指出，民政部門公布的數據顯示，2024年上半年全國結婚登記對數僅為327.5萬對，相較於2013年同期的歷史高峰708萬對已腰斬過半，同時離婚對數卻呈現上升趨勢，相當於每十對新人結婚就有四對伴侶離婚。儘管官方強調要抵制錯誤婚戀觀並建設生育友好型社會，但年輕世代的結婚意願依然持續走低，甚至被預測全年度數據恐跌破600萬大關。

三大推手阻礙婚育：人口縮減、經濟門檻與社交孤島

作者認為，不結婚並非年輕人自私，反而展現了他們審慎評估撫養責任的成熟態度。結婚數下滑的核心在於三大動力：首先是適婚人口基數銳減與初婚年齡延後，從80後到00後世代人口大幅遞減，且年齡越大步入婚姻的機率大幅跌落；其次是成家門檻居高不下，高昂的婚禮花費、房貸與育兒成本讓近八成青年感到沉重壓力，加上大城市中超過五成年輕人成為缺乏社交圈的「孤島青年」，使尋找伴侶變得更加困難。

除了客觀條件的限制，現代青年對婚姻的價值觀也發生深刻變革。作者強調，婚姻已不再是固定的人生腳本，越來越多人將其視為順其自然或可替代的選項，單身也能擁有充實的生活體驗。為挽救低迷的登記率，政府在2024年實施婚姻登記新規，推行全國跨省通辦並取消戶口名簿限制，力圖簡化繁瑣手續以降低結婚門檻，但制度改革能否扭轉長期趨勢仍有待考驗。

after 2000. Since there are fewer. people, the foundation for marriage. registration has naturally shrunk. At. the same time, young people are. marrying later. The threshold for starting a. family makes it impossible for some who. want to marry to do so. Let's talk. about money first; the cost of marriage. leaves many at a loss. childbirth. What do you think it is? Housing or rental costs, education. expenses, dowry or wedding gift. requirements—nearly 80%of people feel. that the stress of finding and keeping. a job is already affecting their dating. and marriage prospects. You see, many. young people aren't just facing a. simple question of whether to marry or. not, but a whole chain of problems: Do. you need to buy a house to get married? Does buying a house mean being tied to. a 30-year mortgage? Should the wedding. have dozens of tables? Should you have. kids after marriage? Who will raise. them? If the pressure mounts while your. income remains unstable, what do you do. ? Every question is followed by. concerns about money, time, and. logistics. It’s easy to tell people. to just get married first, but the. bills won't disappear along with that. advice. Taking it a step further, if. you want to get married, you first have. to meet the right person. Currently,. our country has over 200 million single. people, but the gender gap is a major. issue. Status Report shows that over 80%of. surveyed young people in these cities. are single, with 56.8%categorized as " isolated youth"—meaning they have no. dates, no romantic interests, no. crushes, and no partners of the. opposite sex. If a person's life consists only of. work and going home, with weekends. spent catching up on sleep and a. shrinking social circle, where would. the opportunities for love come from? study, work, marry, have children, and. retire. If you don’t marry, there. must be something wrong with you! Relatives take turns introducing dates,. and parents worry themselves sleepless,. feeling they can't hold their heads up. in public and will be laughed at,. unaware that many young people today. simply don't buy into that pressure. Hey, whose life is this anyway? People. spend their whole lives doing two. things: laughing at others and being. laughed at by others. Unless you have a. cervical spine issue, why wouldn't you. be able to hold your head up? That said. , young people today truly have more. options in life. Some focus on their. careers, some travel everywhere, and. some raise pets, living their lives. with great fulfillment. Emotional. support can also come from friends,. family, and other forms of. companionship; not marrying is no. longer equal to failure, but a personal. choice. In October 2024,. the newly revised marriage registration. regulations were officially implemented. . These regulations did two things:. first, they upgraded marriage. registration from being. cross-provincial to nationwide; second,. they removed the requirement for a. household registration book, allowing. you to get your certificate with just.

an ID card. In the past, young people. working away from home had to take a. train back to their hometowns, bring. their household registration books, and. spend days traveling back and forth. Sometimes, melodramatic scenes would. occur where parents strongly opposed. the couple, forcing them to steal the. registration book from home just to. secretly get the stamp at the civil. affairs bureau. >> If I don't want them to get married,. they won't be able to—believe it or. not? >> I don't believe it. After the new. regulations are implemented, the script. will have to change. But is simplifying. the process actually effective? Perhaps. . In 2022, there were 6.83 million. marriage registrations, which rebounded. to 7.68 million in 2023. However, based. on the data from the second half of. this year, the outlook is not. particularly optimistic. Second, the. measures are quite direct: giving money. to reduce the burden of marriage. Multiple local governments and village. collectives across the country are. already handing out red envelopes to. newlyweds. For example, in Yuliang,. Shanxi, if both parties are first-time. spouses and at least one is a Yuliang. resident, and the woman is 35 years old. or younger, they can receive 1,500 yuan. in cash. Some villages in Foshan have. increased the stakes, offering. newlyweds a one-time reward of 2,500. yuan, with an additional 3,000 for. having a child. In Helan County,. families with zero bride price receive. 5,000, and low bride price families get. 3,000. The best one is Nanling Village. in Guangzhou’s Baiyun District, where. qualified couples can get up to 80,000. yuan, plus another 120,000 for having a. child, for a maximum reward of 200,000. yuan. Some think real money is great,. but others say these measures are just. a drop in the bucket. I think it’s a.

good start; it shows they see the. problem and are thinking of practical. solutions, right? After getting the. marriage certificate, what's the next. step? Raising the kid. So, the third. measure is to improve childcare. services so there's help with raising. children. By the end of 2023, the. number of childcare service. institutions nationwide reached 126,000. , providing about 6.6 million childcare. spots, of which 3.32 million were. affordable, public-benefit spots. This. is actually aimed at solving one of the. biggest pain points for dual-income. families: who will watch the child when. we go to work? If you really can't find. anyone, one parent is forced to quit. their job to take care of them. But if. affordable childcare can keep up,. family pressure could be reduced. significantly. Looking back at the. initial question, why are fewer and. fewer people getting married? It’s. certainly not just because "young. people have given up" or "lack a sense. of responsibility." It is driven by a. combination of factors like a smaller. population, financial issues, and. changing mindsets. Some are waiting for. the right conditions, some for the. right person, and others simply choose. to stay single. Pressuring people to. marry or using moral judgment won’t. work, so what is the real point? We. need to reduce obstacles and, ideally,. create better conditions. Truly. implementing the two-day weekend and. regular working hours gives young. people more time and opportunity,. letting those who want to marry find a. partner and afford a home, while. leaving room for those who choose to be. single. After all, getting a marriage. license takes a day, but building a. family is a life-long commitment, so. prioritizing quality is perfectly. reasonable. Before we wrap up, I’m. A-Jiang. 值得閱讀的理由

  • 從消費習慣、職場文化與穿著舒適度，解析皮鞋如何從身分象徵走向式微。
  • 回顧溫州鞋業的崛起與品質風波，呈現中國皮鞋產業發展的關鍵轉折。
  • 透過奧康、紅蜻蜓、達芙妮與富貴鳥等品牌的興衰，理解傳統企業轉型的困境。

摘要

皮鞋從必備品變成少人穿的鞋

作者指出，過去穿上亮面皮鞋，代表一個人有體面工作、懂得正式場合，也像是在宣告自己有所成就；如今，年輕人上班、約會都更常穿休閒鞋或運動鞋，連西裝也能搭配球鞋。2023年南京街頭調查中，受訪的100名年輕人只有14%穿著皮鞋。消費習慣轉變，也讓老牌鞋企的生意急速萎縮：奧康國際在2020至2023年間累計虧損9億元、關閉約800家門市；紅蜻蜓兩年虧損超過2億元；達芙妮的門市與營收也大幅縮水，富貴鳥則破產退市，成為「品牌還在，公司已倒」的代表案例。

從稀罕奢侈品到溫州鞋業崛起

改革開放初期，多數人穿布鞋、解放鞋或涼鞋，皮鞋是難得的奢侈品。到了1980、1990年代，進城工作、進入辦公室的人愈來愈多，黑皮鞋逐漸成為職業身分與城市生活的象徵。溫州鞋業順勢興起，家庭作坊以價格實惠、款式時髦的鞋子銷往全國；到了1980年代，中國每十雙鞋就有一雙來自溫州。

但快速擴張也帶來品質問題，有些廠商為了壓低價格偷工減料，鞋子容易損壞，甚至被戲稱為「早上鞋」——早上買、下午就壞。1987年，杭州武林廣場焚燒五千多雙劣質溫州皮鞋，多個城市也一度抵制溫州鞋。這場風波反而促使業者重新重視品質與品牌，產業開始從家庭作坊轉向工廠化經營。

皮鞋品牌的黃金年代

1988年，王振滔以3萬元創立奧康，後來將品牌發展成上市公司；曾與他合作的錢金波則另創紅蜻蜓，門市一度遍布全國。福建石獅的富貴鳥也憑藉真皮商務鞋快速成長。2000年至2012年，溫州皮鞋產量從6億雙增至13億雙。當時人們買的不只是鞋，更是體面與地位；西裝搭配一雙擦亮的黑皮鞋，幾乎就是職場成功的標準形象。

職場變休閒，皮鞋失去光環

近年皮鞋市場占比快速下滑，運動鞋市場則持續擴大。作者歸納出皮鞋失寵的兩大原因。首先，穿皮鞋的正式場合減少：企業服裝規定逐漸放寬，商務休閒穿搭也日益普遍，運動鞋出現在辦公室與正式場合不再突兀。當企業領袖也能穿球鞋出席公開活動，皮鞋便不再是證明地位的必要符號，逐漸失去「職場剛需」與「身分象徵」兩張王牌。

其次，舒適度成為無法忽視的弱點。許多正式皮鞋走路半小時就讓雙腳疲累，悶熱、磨腳與擠腳等問題也常被消費者提起；對通勤、久站或整天走動的人來說，穿著不適很容易變成折磨。高跟鞋的處境更明顯，許多工廠已停產高跟鞋，日常穿高跟鞋的女性也只剩少數。曾經代表優雅的高跟鞋，如今往往只在不得不穿的場合出現。休閒鞋與運動鞋因此接手了大量需求。

傳統品牌轉型，難在改變消費者印象

面對市場轉向，奧康與紅蜻蜓嘗試擴大產品類別、吸引年輕客群。紅蜻蜓推出德比鞋、勃肯風涼鞋與復古運動鞋，執行長也親自直播帶貨，但轉型成效有限，近年仍面臨虧損；奧康則透過子品牌康龍發展年輕休閒鞋款，然而在相近價格帶，年輕消費者還有安踏、耐吉等選擇，銷售表現不理想。

這些案例凸顯傳統鞋企共同的難題：改變款式容易，改變品牌印象卻很難。不少年輕人仍把它們視為「爸爸穿的鞋」，而休閒鞋市場早已聚集大量運動與潮流品牌，老牌鞋企想搶回年輕消費者並不容易。作者由此指出，皮鞋品牌的困境不只是產品變化，更牽涉消費者認知與市場競爭格局的改變。

By 2019, the former. listed company went bankrupt and. delisted, with the brand fading away—. a classic case of "the brand lives, but. the company dies." So the question is,. how did leather shoes become popular in. China, why did they fall out of favor,. and why is the turnaround for shoe. brands so difficult? Looking back. Let’s first talk about how leather. shoes rose to prominence. Let’s wind.

the clock back to the early days of. reform and opening up. What were most. Chinese people wearing then? Cloth. shoes, Jiefang shoes (rubber-soled work. shoes), sandals, and some people even. wore homemade shoes. Back then, leather. shoes were definitely a rare luxury. Being able to wear a pair of shiny. leather shoes made one look trendy and. respectable, like someone who had seen. the world and was living a good life. By the 80s and 90s, more people were. moving to cities for work and entering. offices for business activities. At. that time, a pair of black leather. shoes sent a clear message: "I’ve. started a professional job, I live in. the city, and I am a person of status." The Wenzhou shoe industry took off by. riding this wave of demand. In the. early days of opening up, Wenzhou saw. an emergence of numerous family. workshops. With a few machines set up. in a room, the whole family would make. shoes together and then go out to sell. them. Back then, the market economy was. just starting and goods were scarce. Wenzhou shoes were cheap and stylish,. so they quickly sold across the whole. country. By the 1980s, one out of every. ten pairs of shoes in China was made in. Wenzhou, and a large portion of them. were leather shoes. However, this. unbridled growth also sowed the seeds. of hidden danger. To compete on price,. many manufacturers began cutting. corners, using cardboard for insoles. and inferior glue for outsoles, which. would soon come apart. These shoes were. once mockingly called "morning shoes," meaning if you bought them in the. morning, they’d be broken by the. afternoon; if you were lucky, they. might last a week. On August 8, 1987, a. massive bonfire was lit in Hangzhou's. Wulin Square, burning over 5,000 pairs. of inferior Wenzhou leather shoes. Subsequently, over a dozen cities. including Shanghai, Nanjing, and Wuhan.

banned Wenzhou shoes, branding them as. "shoddy" or "low-quality." Yet, the. Wenzhou footwear industry didn't. collapse; instead, this fire served as. a wake-up call for the city's. manufacturers, with over 70 factory. owners joining forces to prioritize. quality, supported by the local. government's efforts to rebuild their. reputation. With a new focus, workshops. began upgrading into factories,. shifting the competition from price to. branding, which is exactly how. companies like Aokang rose to. prominence. In 1988, the year after the. shoe-burning incident, Wang Zhentao. founded Aokang with 30,000 yuan; growing from a family workshop to a. listed company on the Shanghai Stock. Exchange by 2012, it achieved annual. revenue of 3.455 billion yuan and a. profit of 513 million, with over 5,300. stores nationwide—I still remember. their slogan, "Wear Aokang, walk the. world." Qian Jinbo, who had partnered. with Wang Zhentao in the early days,. later struck out on his own to found. Red Dragonfly, expanding his stores. across the country to a peak of over. 4,300 locations. From 2000 to 2012,. Wenzhou's leather shoe production. jumped from 600 million to 1.3 billion. pairs; based on the population at the. time, that meant every single person in. China effectively owned a pair of. Wenzhou leather shoes. Outside of. Wenzhou, Fujian’s Shishi also saw the. rise of Fuguiniao, which quickly grew. its genuine leather business shoe line,. listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. in 2013, and boasted over 3,000 retail. outlets with annual revenue nearing 2.3. billion. It was truly the golden age of. leather shoes; a polished black pair. paired with a suit was the definition. of professional success for many, as. people were buying not just a pair of. shoes, but a sense of decency and. status. However, over the past decade,.

the rules of the game have changed, and. leather shoes have gradually faded from. the mainstream market and been. marginalized by the younger generation. Their market share fell from 41.7%in. 2016 to 15.3%in 2020, with some. institutions predicting it will drop. below 9%by 2023. So, what about sports. shoes? The market size reached 125.5. billion in 2025, a year-on-year. increase of 11%, leaving leather shoes. far behind. Why have leather shoes. fallen out of favor over the past. decade or so? There are two main. reasons. First, the occasions requiring. leather shoes have diminished. Previously, the largest market for. leather shoes was the business. workplace; companies had formal dress. codes, and individuals wanted to look. professional, making leather shoes a. standard for workers. But now,. workplace attire is increasingly. relaxed. A 2024 survey showed that only. 42%of companies require employees to. wear uniforms, professional attire, or. formal wear—less than half. In some. relaxed internet companies, no one. cares if you wear slippers or sneakers. to work, and business casual is now. popular even in the finance and. information industries; a dress shirt. paired with sneakers doesn't look out. of place. More importantly, in this. process, leather shoes lost their. monopoly on status and success. Look at. Lei Jun wearing sneakers to a product. launch or Tim Cook wearing them as an. executive; since business titans don't. need leather shoes to prove their. status, ordinary people have even less. reason to mistreat their feet. Thus,. leather shoes gradually lost their two. trump cards: the rigid demand of the. workplace and their unique value as a. status symbol. Once they lost their. halo, they had to compete on the. product itself, exposing their greatest. weakness: discomfort. Many formal.

leather shoes make your feet tired. after walking for half an hour. A. survey found that on social media, the. terms "blisters,""stuffy," and "pinched. feet" regarding leather shoes were. mentioned 78,000 times. Nowadays, many. people commute by subway, stand for. meetings, or are on their feet all day,. so any discomfort is amplified into. torture. This is even more prominent. with women's high heels. Data from the. China Leather Industry Association. shows that about 90%of factories. nationwide have shut down their. high-heel production lines, and only 4%. of women still wear them daily. High. heels have shifted from a standard of. elegance to a "beauty tax," worn only. when necessary. Most of this vacated. market has been captured by casual and. athletic shoes; notably, nearly 80%of. young people own over five pairs of. sneakers, and over 60%wear them every. day. Seeing consumers switch footwear,. traditional leather shoe companies are. getting anxious. How can they save. themselves? There are mainly two paths. The first is changing what they sell,. expanding product categories to appeal. to young people. Red Dragonfly and. Aokang have taken this path. Red. Dragonfly has started making Derby. shoes, Birkenstock-style sandals, and. retro sneakers, with the CEO even. personally hosting livestreams to sell. products. However, the transformation. results have been disappointing, with. losses in both 2024 and 2025; the 140. million loss in 2025 marked the worst. performance since going public. Fortunately, they barely broke even in. the first half of 2026 with a profit of. 8.95 million, but the net profit. excluding non-recurring items was only. 160,000, meaning day-to-day operations. were essentially not making money. Then. there's Aokang, which also tried to. find growth through rejuvenation. Its. subsidiary, Kanglong, focuses on.

youthful casual wear, with products. mainly priced between 399 and 599 yuan. However, at this price point, young. people have various other options like. Anta and Nike, and as a result, sales. have indeed flopped. In 2020,. Kanglong's revenue was only 102 million. yuan, a year-on-year plunge of 45%,. accounting for just 5.5%of the group's. total revenue, leaving it with little. market presence. Red Dragonfly and. Aokang both hit the same hurdle: it's. easy to change styles, but hard to. change the brand image. In the eyes of. many young people, they are still just. shoes for "dads," and the casual market. is already crowded with sports and. trendy brands—winning young consumers. from them is not that simple. Also,. even if the styles keep up, the supply. chain is another major hurdle. Leather. shoes used to have just a few styles. produced in large batches, but now it's. about chasing trends, emphasizing. small-batch, multi-style, and rapid. testing. It truly. goes to show: speed is the only way to. stay unbeatable. So, shoe. transformation isn't just about. changing a few styles; whether young. people accept the brand and whether the. factory can keep up are both major. challenges. Besides expanding product. categories, there is a second typical. path, where the way shoe companies make. money is also changing, and Daphne is. the most classic example. In 2019,. Daphne closed over 2,300 retail. locations in one go, gradually moving. away from the old model of large-scale.

direct operation and shifting focus to. franchising, wholesale, and brand. licensing. So, how did that turn out? In 2022, Daphne's revenue reached 364. million yuan, marking four consecutive. years of growth; they have indeed. recovered. But compared to their peak. revenue of over 10 billion, it's just a. fraction, and if you break down the. income, over 90%comes from wholesale. and brand licensing, with retail. revenue from selling their own shoes at. only 24 million yuan. What does this. tell us? Simply put, in the past, they. relied mainly on company-owned stores,. selling shoes through thousands of. locations; but now, they act more as. intermediaries supplying downstream. retailers or using direct. white-labeling. The brand remains, but. the business model has shifted. Whether. expanding product lines or changing. models, the reality remains the same:. the old way of making money through. business dress shoes and aggressive. store expansion is becoming harder and. harder to sustain. Finally, if we look. back at the status of leather shoes. over the past 40 years, it actually. reflects the changing consumption. concepts of the Chinese people. In the. early days of reform and opening up, a. pair of proper leather shoes was meant. to show others that life was improving. As the market matured and mass-market. brands emerged, leather shoes became a. staple of professional and social. identity—essential for work, client. meetings, and weddings. But today, when. people buy shoes, the first question is. : will my feet hurt after walking all. day? Is it convenient for taking the. subway? Can it match my personal style? Leather shoes haven't disappeared; they’ve just shifted from being a. daily essential to a situational choice. . In the past, a shoe only needed to. make you look decent to sell nationwide. . Today, it must also be comfortable.

and stylish for it to be worth the. price and generate profit. I'm A-Jiang. That's all for this video. Please. follow, and see you next time. Y.

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入剖析民宿行業從十年暴漲20倍到入住率慘跌的真實市場變化。
  • 揭露網紅民宿價格高昂背後隱藏的衛生盲盒與照片造假等行業亂象。
  • 分析年輕人消費觀念轉變，從追求包裝拍照到回歸理性與品質的關鍵原因。

摘要

從熱潮到冰點：年輕人放棄網紅民宿

作者指出，過去年輕人旅遊時熱衷於預訂具有網紅打卡風格的民宿，帶動民宿訂單量暴增。然而最近兩年形勢大逆轉，許多旅客轉而選擇清潔靠譜的連鎖酒店。數據顯示，熱門旅遊城市的民宿入住率大幅下滑，部分商家甚至難以維繫經營，整體行業的平均入住率已降至低點，伴隨著大量空置率與口碑下滑。

十年暴漲20倍：低門檻與高回報的盲目擴張

作者回顧了民宿行業的發展歷程。自2015年共享住宿模式進入中國市場後，民宿被賦予情懷與風尚，吸引大量年輕人投入創業。由於其具有低門檻、高回報的特性，相關企業數量在十年內擴張了近20倍。節假日期間房價更是數倍翻漲，進而引發了一場盲目的投資狂歡與擴張熱潮。

亂象頻出：衛生盲盒與AI假圖引爆信任危機

作者分析了民宿失去吸引力的主要原因。首先是衛生狀況堪比開盲盒，缺乏統一標準與監督，導致衛生環境惡劣的投訴居高不下；其次是虛假宣傳與套路嚴重，商家利用AI技術生成美照、甚至實行「AB房」套路欺騙消費者，嚴重破壞了消費者的信任基石。

千店一面與理性消費：品質與服務才是硬道理

作者提到，民宿產業正面臨嚴重的同質化問題。大量民宿套用相同的網紅裝修模板，讓旅客產生審美疲勞。同時，年輕人的消費觀念逐漸回歸理性，不再願意為虛有其表的「網紅濾鏡」溢價買單。作者強調，民宿若要長遠發展，最終必須擺脫噱頭，回歸到優質的產品品質與服務體驗。
